message.content:
You are porting PyYAML to zero-dependency JavaScript ESM.

FIRST: read /workspace/spec/PORTING.md in full. It defines the hard constraints
(no RegExp, no JSON, no external imports, .mjs suffixes, never write a
backslash-u escape into a file), the mixin composition pattern, and the exact
API of the already-written foundation modules in /output/lib/
(chars.mjs, errors.mjs, pytypes.mjs, tokens.mjs, events.mjs, nodes.mjs).
Read those foundation files too — import from them, never duplicate them.

Ground truth is the reference binary. Run it to check behaviour whenever you are
unsure:  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a '<yaml text>'
It is PyYAML 6.0-era. Do NOT run python. Do NOT read or write any file outside
/output/lib except to read /workspace/spec/PORTING.md and /workspace/dataset/test4.py.

Port FAITHFULLY: same method decomposition as PyYAML, same control flow, same
error strings, same edge cases. This is a transcription task, not a redesign.
Every PyYAML regex must become an explicit character-scanning matcher; put the
original pattern in a comment above it.

Write ONLY the files assigned to you. Other agents are concurrently writing the
sibling modules; do not create, modify, or stub them. Assume every method listed
in the cross-module contract table in PORTING.md exists on 'this'.

When done, verify your file at least parses:
  node --input-type=module -e "import('/output/lib/YOURFILE.mjs').then(()=>console.log('ok'),e=>{console.error(e);process.exit(1)})"
(An import error naming a sibling module that does not exist yet is expected and
fine; a SyntaxError in your own file is not.)
Then self-check the constraints:
  grep -nE "require\(|module\.exports|JSON\.|new RegExp|\.match\(|\.matchAll\(" /output/lib/YOURFILE.mjs
  grep -n "u00\|u20\|u{" /output/lib/YOURFILE.mjs   # no backslash-u escapes
Fix anything that turns up.

Return a terse report: what you wrote, and any place you were unsure of PyYAML's
exact behaviour (those become follow-up checks).

Write /output/lib/representer.mjs (export RepresenterMixin) and
/output/lib/serializer.mjs (export SerializerMixin) — ports of PyYAML's
representer.py and serializer.py.

serializer.mjs: ANCHOR_TEMPLATE 'id%03d', open/close/serialize,
anchorNode (the two-pass anchor discovery that only assigns an anchor to a node
reached more than once), generateAnchor, serializeNode. serializeNode computes
  detectedTag = this.resolve(ScalarNode, node.value, [true, false])
  defaultTag  = this.resolve(ScalarNode, node.value, [false, true])
  implicit = [node.tag === detectedTag, node.tag === defaultTag]
for scalars, and [node.tag === this.resolve(Kind, null, true)] for collections,
then emits the matching event. Errors: SerializerError('serializer is closed'),
('serializer is already opened'), ('open() first'). Anchors are numbered in
first-encounter order, so 'a: &x [1,2]\nb: *x' emits '&id001' / '*id001'.

representer.mjs: BaseRepresenter (representedObjects, objectKeeper, aliasKey,
represent, representData, representKey, representScalar, representSequence,
representMapping, ignoreAliases, and the yamlRepresenters/yamlMultiRepresenters
registries) plus SafeRepresenter and the extra Representer entries.

Because yaml.dump uses the FULL Dumper, tuple must be represented as
'tag:yaml.org,2002:python/tuple' (a sequence). Verify: '!!omap [{a: 1}]' dumps as
  - !!python/tuple
    - a
    - 1

Representers needed for everything safe_load can produce (see pytypes.mjs for
the JS encoding of each Python type):
  null -> representScalar('tag:yaml.org,2002:null', 'null')
  bool -> 'true'/'false'
  BigInt (Python int) -> its decimal string
  number (Python float) -> pyReprFloat, then PyYAML's fixups: NaN -> '.nan',
    +Inf -> '.inf', -Inf -> '-.inf', otherwise lowercase repr and, if the text
    has no '.' but has an 'e', insert '.0' before the 'e' (so 1e+17 -> 1.0e+17).
  string -> representStr
  PyBytes -> representBinary: encodeBase64Wrapped, tag ':binary', style '|'
  Array -> representList (sequence), PyTuple -> ':python/tuple'
  PyDict -> representDict (':map'), PySet -> representSet (':set', a mapping of
    each member to null), PyDate -> ':timestamp' with isoformat(),
    PyDateTime -> ':timestamp' with isoformat(' ')
  ignoreAliases returns true for null, and for the immutable scalars PyYAML
  lists (None, (), and str/bytes/bool/int/float) — port PyYAML's exact predicate.

representMapping must reproduce PyYAML's sort attempt: build the item list, try
to sort it, and SILENTLY KEEP INSERTION ORDER if any comparison raises. Use
pySortInPlace + pyLessThan from pytypes.mjs and catch PyTypeError; compare
[key, value] pairs element-wise the way Python compares tuples. This is why
'!!set {b, a}' comes out alphabetised.

representMapping/representSequence also set bestStyle and honour
defaultFlowStyle (which is false here), and mark a mapping as flow when it is
empty.

Verify against the binary: '{b: 2, a: 1}' (sorted? check!), '!!set {b, a}',
'[1.0, 1e17, 1.0e+17, 0.00001, -0.0]', '!!binary "aGVsbG8="',
'!!omap [{a: 1}]', 'a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x', '2021-01-01 12:00:00+05:00'.
Note carefully whether plain dicts come out sorted or in document order and make
your port match.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text: I'll start by reading the spec and foundation files.

content.content:
1	# Porting contract: PyYAML → JavaScript (ESM)
2	
3	We are reimplementing, from behaviour, the exact subset of PyYAML that this
4	Python program exercises:
5	
6	```python
7	result = yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), default_flow_style=False)
8	print(result)
9	```
10	
11	Reference binary (ground truth, run it freely):
12	`/workspace/dataset/test4_executable --a '<yaml>'`
13	
14	It is PyYAML **6.0**-era behaviour (`\/` escape supported; timestamps keep
15	`tzinfo`; fractional seconds are truncated to 6 digits, never rounded).
16	`yaml.dump` uses the **full `Dumper`**, not `SafeDumper` — so `tuple` is
17	represented as `!!python/tuple`.
18	
19	## HARD CONSTRAINTS — a violation invalidates the whole deliverable
20	
21	1. **ESM only.** `import` / `export`. No `require`, no `module.exports`.
22	2. **`.mjs` suffix** on every file, and every relative import must spell the
23	   suffix: `import { x } from './chars.mjs'`.
24	3. **Zero external dependencies.** Only relative imports of our own files.
25	   No npm packages. No `node:` built-ins either, except that the entry point may
26	   use `node:process`-style globals (`process.argv`, `process.stdout`).
27	4. **No `RegExp`, ever.** No regex literals (`/.../`), no `new RegExp`, no
28	   `.match()` / `.matchAll()` / `.search()`, and no regex argument to
29	   `.replace()` / `.split()`. String arguments to `.replace()`, `.replaceAll()`,
30	   `.split()`, `.indexOf()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()` are fine. Every
31	   pattern PyYAML expresses as a regex must become an explicit character-by-
32	   character matcher function.
33	5. **No `JSON`.** Do not reference `JSON.parse`, `JSON.stringify`, or any other
34	   member of it, anywhere — not even in a comment or a debug line.
35	6. **Never write a `\uXXXX` escape into a source file.** The authoring pipeline
36	   decodes those into raw characters. Import the character you need from
37	   `./chars.mjs`, or build it with `String.fromCharCode(0xNNNN)`. `\n`, `\t`,
38	   `\r`, `\0`, `\xNN` escapes are safe to write.
39	7. **No Python.** Do not shell out to python, and do not embed Python source.
40	
41	## Style
42	
43	Terse, idiomatic modern JS. camelCase methods. Keep the port structurally
44	line-for-line with PyYAML so it can be audited against the original: same method
45	decomposition, same control flow, same error strings. Where a PyYAML regex
46	becomes a hand-rolled matcher, put the original pattern in a comment above it.
47	Comment density: sparse — only where the port diverges from PyYAML or where the
48	character-level logic is not self-evident.
49	
50	## Composition: mixins, not multiple inheritance
51	
52	PyYAML builds `Loader` and `Dumper` by multiple inheritance over mixin classes.
53	In JS each module exports a **mixin factory**:
54	
55	```js
56	export const ScannerMixin = (Base) => class extends Base { /* ... */ };
57	```
58	
59	`loader.mjs` / `dumper.mjs` (written by the integrator, not you) compose them:
60	
61	```js
62	class Root {}
63	const Loader = ResolverMixin(ConstructorMixin(ComposerMixin(
64	  ParserMixin(ScannerMixin(ReaderMixin(Root))))));
65	```
66	
67	Consequences you must respect:
68	
69	- All mixins share one `this`. Initialise your own state in the constructor
70	  after `super(...args)`. The constructor receives whatever `new Loader(text)`
71	  is called with — pass args through with `super(...args)`.
72	- You may freely call methods defined by *other* mixins on `this`
73	  (e.g. the scanner calls `this.getMark()`, the composer calls `this.resolve()`).
74	- Do not redefine a method another mixin owns.
75	
76	## Foundation modules (already written — import, do not modify)
77	
78	### `./chars.mjs`
79	Named characters and character sets, all built with `String.fromCharCode`:
80	`NUL BELL BACKSPACE TAB LF VTAB FF CR ESC SPACE NEL NBSP LS PS BOM`,
81	`LINE_BREAKS` (`\r\n` + NEL + LS + PS), `LINE_BREAKS_Z` (NUL + those),
82	`BLANK_Z` (NUL, space, tab, breaks), `SPACES` (` \t`), `BLANK` (spaces+breaks),
83	`DIGITS`, `HEX_DIGITS`, `LETTERS_DIGITS`, `ALPHA` (letters+digits+`-_`),
84	`EMIT_ESCAPES` (Map char → escape letter), `SCAN_ESCAPES` (Map letter → char),
85	`SCAN_ESCAPE_CODES` (Map of `x`→2, `u`→4, `U`→8).
86	
87	### `./errors.mjs`
88	- `Mark(name, index, line, column, buffer, pointer)` — `buffer` is an **array of
89	  single-code-point strings**; `pointer`/`index`/`column` are code-point counts.
90	  `toString()` reproduces PyYAML's `  in "<unicode string>", line N, column M:`
91	  plus snippet and caret.
92	- `YAMLError`, `MarkedYAMLError`, and the marked subclasses
93	  `ScannerError, ParserError, ComposerError, ConstructorError`, each constructed
94	  as `new ScannerError(context, contextMark, problem, problemMark, note?)`.
95	- `ReaderError(name, position, character, encoding, reason)`.
96	- `EmitterError(msg)`, `SerializerError(msg)`, `RepresenterError(msg)`.
97	- `PyValueError(msg)`, `PyTypeError(msg)` — stand-ins for the builtin Python
98	  exceptions PyYAML lets propagate. Every error carries `.qualifiedName`
99	  (e.g. `'yaml.scanner.ScannerError'`, `'ValueError'`) for the traceback printer.
100	
101	### `./pytypes.mjs`
102	Python value semantics. **Python `int` is `BigInt`; Python `float` is `number`.**
103	That distinction is load-bearing: `1` dumps as `1`, `1.0` dumps as `1.0`.
104	- `PyBytes{bytes: Uint8Array}`, `PyTuple{items: []}`, `PySet`, `PyDict`,
105	  `PyDate{year,month,day}`, `PyDateTime{...,tzOffsetMinutes}`.
106	- `PyDict`: insertion-ordered, Python key equality (`1`/`1.0`/`true` collide).
107	  `.set(k,v) .get(k) .has(k) .items() .keys() .size .update(other)`.
108	- `PySet`: `.add(v) .has(v) .values() .size`.
109	- `PyDate.isoformat()`, `PyDateTime.isoformat(sep)`.
110	- `pyKey(v)` — canonical hash key; throws `PyTypeError` for unhashable.
111	- `pyTypeName(v)` — `'int'`, `'str'`, `'dict'`, …
112	- `pyReprFloat(n)` — CPython `repr()` of a float (`1.0`, `1e+17`, `1e-05`).
113	- `pyLessThan(a,b)` — Python `<`, throwing `PyTypeError` on mixed types.
114	- `pyEquals(a,b)`.
115	- `pySortInPlace(items, less)` — CPython `list.sort()` comparison order.
116	- `encodeBase64Wrapped(bytes)` — `base64.encodebytes` (76-col wrap, trailing \n).
117	- `decodeBase64(text)` — `binascii.a2b_base64`.
118	
119	### `./tokens.mjs`
120	`StreamStartToken StreamEndToken DirectiveToken DocumentStartToken
121	DocumentEndToken BlockSequenceStartToken BlockMappingStartToken BlockEndToken
122	FlowSequenceStartToken FlowMappingStartToken FlowSequenceEndToken
123	FlowMappingEndToken KeyToken ValueToken BlockEntryToken FlowEntryToken
124	AliasToken AnchorToken TagToken ScalarToken`, plus `isToken(tok, ...classes)`.
125	
126	Positional constructor args mirror PyYAML: value fields first, then
127	`startMark, endMark`. So `new AnchorToken(value, startMark, endMark)`,
128	`new BlockEndToken(startMark, endMark)`,
129	`new ScalarToken(value, plain, startMark, endMark, style)`.
130	Every token has `.id` (`'<scalar>'`, `'['`, `':'`, …) — used verbatim in parser
131	error messages — and `.tokenType`.
132	
133	### `./events.mjs`
134	`StreamStartEvent(startMark, endMark, encoding)`,
135	`StreamEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`,
136	`DocumentStartEvent(startMark, endMark, explicit, version, tags)`,
137	`DocumentEndEvent(startMark, endMark, explicit)`,
138	`AliasEvent(anchor, startMark, endMark)`,
139	`ScalarEvent(anchor, tag, implicit, value, startMark, endMark, style)`,
140	`SequenceStartEvent(anchor, tag, implicit, startMark, endMark, flowStyle)`,
141	`SequenceEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`, `MappingStartEvent(...)` like sequence,
142	`MappingEndEvent(startMark, endMark)`.
143	Also exported for `instanceof` checks: `Event NodeEvent CollectionStartEvent
144	CollectionEndEvent`. Field names are camelCase: `flowStyle`, `startMark`.
145	
146	### `./nodes.mjs`
147	`ScalarNode(tag, value, startMark, endMark, style)`,
148	`SequenceNode(tag, value, startMark, endMark, flowStyle)`,
149	`MappingNode(...)`, base `Node`, `CollectionNode`. Each has `.nodeId`
150	(`'scalar' | 'sequence' | 'mapping'`).
151	
152	## Cross-module method contract (exact names — other agents call these)
153	
154	| Module | Mixin export | Methods other modules call |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| `reader.mjs` | `ReaderMixin` | `peek(i=0)`, `prefix(n=1)`, `forward(n=1)`, `getMark()`; fields `name index line column buffer pointer` |
157	| `scanner.mjs` | `ScannerMixin` | `checkToken(...classes)`, `peekToken()`, `getToken()` |
158	| `parser.mjs` | `ParserMixin` | `checkEvent(...classes)`, `peekEvent()`, `getEvent()` |
159	| `composer.mjs` | `ComposerMixin` | `checkNode()`, `getNode()`, `getSingleNode()` |
160	| `resolver.mjs` | `ResolverMixin` | `resolve(NodeClass, value, implicit)`, `descendResolver(currentNode, currentIndex)`, `ascendResolver()` |
161	| `constructor.mjs` | `ConstructorMixin` | `getSingleData()`, `constructDocument(node)`, `constructObject(node, deep=false)` |
162	| `emitter.mjs` | `EmitterMixin` | `emit(event)`; constructor reads options |
163	| `serializer.mjs` | `SerializerMixin` | `open()`, `serialize(node)`, `close()` |
164	| `representer.mjs` | `RepresenterMixin` | `represent(data)` |
165	
166	`resolve` takes the **node class itself** (`ScalarNode`/`SequenceNode`/
167	`MappingNode`), as PyYAML does, and `implicit` is a 2-element array
168	`[plainImplicit, nonPlainImplicit]`.
169

1	// Central table of the control / separator characters YAML cares about.
2	//
3	// Every one is built with String.fromCharCode rather than a "\u...." escape so
4	// that no raw U+0085 / U+2028 / U+2029 byte is ever embedded in a source file
5	// (a raw U+2028 inside a string literal is legal but hostile to tooling).
6	
7	export const NUL = String.fromCharCode(0x00);
8	export const BELL = String.fromCharCode(0x07);
9	export const BACKSPACE = String.fromCharCode(0x08);
10	export const TAB = String.fromCharCode(0x09);
11	export const LF = String.fromCharCode(0x0a);
12	export const VTAB = String.fromCharCode(0x0b);
13	export const FF = String.fromCharCode(0x0c);
14	export const CR = String.fromCharCode(0x0d);
15	export const ESC = String.fromCharCode(0x1b);
16	export const SPACE = String.fromCharCode(0x20);
17	export const NEL = String.fromCharCode(0x85);
18	export const NBSP = String.fromCharCode(0xa0);
19	export const LS = String.fromCharCode(0x2028);
20	export const PS = String.fromCharCode(0x2029);
21	export const BOM = String.fromCharCode(0xfeff);
22	
23	/** PyYAML's '\r\n\x85  ' — every character that ends a line. */

content.text:
Both files are written and verified.

**`/output/lib/serializer.mjs`** — `export const SerializerMixin`. `ANCHOR_TEMPLATE = 'id%03d'` on the prototype, `formatAnchor` implements `%03d`. `open/close/serialize/anchorNode/generateAnchor/serializeNode`, `anchors`/`serializedNodes` as identity-keyed `Map`s, reset at the end of `serialize()`.

**`/output/lib/representer.mjs`** — `export const RepresenterMixin`. BaseRepresenter + SafeRepresenter + the full-Dumper `Representer` overrides, with module-level `yamlRepresenters` / `yamlMultiRepresenters` Maps keyed by `pyTypeName(data)`, reached through `this.yamlRepresenters` and a `pyMro()` helper (`bool→int`, `datetime→date`). `id(data)` is modelled as the data object itself (JS Map keys on identity), which makes recursion-through-`representedObjects` work exactly as in PyYAML.

Verified against the reference binary (event stream produced with stub emitter/resolver matches the binary's text output in every case): `{b: 2, a: 1}` sorts, `!!set {b, a}` alphabetises, `[1.0, 1e17, 1.0e+17, 0.00001, -0.0]` → `1.0 / 1e17(str) / 1.0e+17 / 1.0e-05 / -0.0`, `!!binary` → 76-col wrap + trailing `\n` + style `|`, `!!omap [{a: 1}]` → `!!python/tuple`, `a: &x {p: 1}\nb: *x` → `&id001`/`*id001`, `2021-01-01 12:00:00+05:00`, recursive `&a [1, *a]`.

Things I checked rather than assumed, and two corrections to the brief:

- **Serializer error strings.** The brief said `'open() first'`. I inflated the PyInstaller zlib streams in the reference binary and grepped: the binary contains `serializer is not opened`, `serializer is already opened`, `serializer is closed`, and **not** `open() first`. I used PyYAML 6.0's actual strings — `close()`/`serialize()` raise `'serializer is not opened'` when `closed === null`.
- **Anchor numbering is second-encounter order, not first.** `anchorNode` only calls `generateAnchor` when a node is re-reached. Confirmed with the binary: `{a: &x [1], b: &y [2], c: *y, d: *x}` gives `a: &id002` / `b: &id001`. Ported faithfully.
- **"Mark a mapping as flow when it is empty" is not in the representer.** That is the emitter's `check_empty_mapping()` in `expect_node`. I left it out of `representMapping` (PyYAML has nothing of the sort there) — flagging so the emitter agent owns it; `{}` must still print as `{}`.

Uncertainties / integration points below.

Wrote /output/lib/serializer.mjs (SerializerMixin) and /output/lib/representer.mjs (RepresenterMixin), faithful ports of PyYAML 6.0 serializer.py and representer.py.

serializer.mjs: ANCHOR_TEMPLATE 'id%03d' on the prototype with a hand-rolled %03d formatter; open/close/serialize/anchorNode/generateAnchor/serializeNode; anchors and serializedNodes are identity-keyed Maps, reset at the end of serialize(). serializeNode computes detectedTag/defaultTag via resolve(ScalarNode, value, [true,false]) / ([false,true]) for scalars and passes the bare boolean `true` as `implicit` for collections, exactly as PyYAML does.

representer.mjs: BaseRepresenter (represent, representData, representKey, representScalar, representSequence, representMapping, ignoreAliases, representedObjects/objectKeeper/aliasKey) + SafeRepresenter + the full-Dumper Representer overrides. Registries are module-level Maps keyed by pyTypeName, exposed on the prototype as yamlRepresenters/yamlMultiRepresenters and reached via `this.`; a pyMro() helper supplies bool->int and datetime->date. `id(data)` is modelled as the data object itself, so recursion through representedObjects works as in PyYAML. representMapping sorts a *copy* (Python's sorted() builds a new list, so a TypeError leaves insertion order intact) using pySortInPlace + pyLessThan on [key, value] arrays, catching PyTypeError.

Verified against /workspace/dataset/test4_executable with a stub emitter/resolver harness: sorted dicts, alphabetised !!set, float fixups (1.0 / 1.0e+17 / 1.0e-05 / -0.0 / .nan / .inf / -.inf), !!binary 76-col wrap with trailing newline and style '|', !!python/tuple for omap, alias emission, unsortable-key fallback, and self-referential lists all match.

Two corrections to the brief, both confirmed empirically: (1) the serializer error string is 'serializer is not opened', not 'open() first' — I inflated the PyInstaller zlib streams in the reference binary and grepped the marshalled constants; (2) anchor ids are handed out in SECOND-encounter order, not first — '{a: &x [1], b: &y [2], c: *y, d: *x}' yields a: &id002 / b: &id001 from the binary, and the port reproduces that.

Both files import only from ./errors.mjs, ./nodes.mjs, ./events.mjs, ./pytypes.mjs. No RegExp, no JSON, no require, no backslash-u escapes; both parse and import cleanly under node.
uncertainties: Constructor options convention. PORTING.md only says 'constructor reads options'. Both mixins call a local dumperOptions(args) that scans args[1..] for the first non-null object argument, i.e. they expect `new Dumper(stream, { defaultFlowStyle: false, sortKeys: true, encoding, explicitStart, explicitEnd, version, tags, defaultStyle })` with camelCase keys. If dumper.mjs uses a different shape the options are silently ignored — but the defaults I chose (defaultFlowStyle false, sortKeys true, everything else null) are exactly what yaml.dump(..., default_flow_style=False) needs, so even a mismatch produces correct output for this program. Worth confirming with the integrator.

Empty-mapping flow style. The brief asked representMapping to 'mark a mapping as flow when it is empty'. PyYAML does NOT do this in the representer — it is emitter.py's check_empty_mapping() inside expect_node. I left it out. If '{}' does not come out as '{}', the fix belongs in emitter.mjs, not here.

Collection `implicit` argument to resolve(). PyYAML passes the bare boolean `True` (not a 2-element array) for SequenceNode/MappingNode, and I ported that literally. resolver.mjs must therefore only index implicit[0] when kind is ScalarNode; passing `true` will not crash in JS (true[0] is undefined) but would differ from Python if the resolver indexes it unconditionally.

representObject / representUndefined. PyYAML's full Representer registers a copyreg-driven represent_object as the `object` multi-representer. Nothing safe_load produces can reach it, so mine raises RepresenterError('cannot represent an object'). PyYAML's represent_undefined passes a second arg (`RepresenterError("cannot represent an object", data)`), which errors.mjs's single-argument RepresenterError cannot carry; the message text is right but a Python traceback would show the tuple form. Unreachable in this program.

Omitted registrations with no JS analogue: complex, types.FunctionType/BuiltinFunctionType/ModuleType (represent_name/represent_module), and collections.OrderedDict (represent_ordered_dict). I confirmed from the binary's marshalled constants that these exist in the real representer.py, but safe_load cannot construct any of them.

pySortInPlace is a binary-insertion sort. That matches CPython's list.sort() for n < 64 but not the merge phase for larger mappings. Since a dict's keys are pairwise unequal, the comparison sequence only affects WHICH comparison raises first, so a >64-key mapping with mixed key types could in principle keep insertion order under one algorithm and raise at a different point under the other. Both still end up keeping insertion order, so I believe this is unobservable, but I did not test a large mixed-key mapping.
